        "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict signups to Google OAuth only\n-- Purpose: Blocks email/password signups and OTP signups, only allows Google OAuth\n-- This ensures all new accounts must be created via Google OAuth\n\n-- Create before_user_created hook in public schema to only allow Google OAuth signups\n-- Blocks email/password signups and other OAuth providers\n-- Uses public schema instead of auth schema\ncreate or replace function public.before_user_created_hook(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_provider text;\n  v_encrypted_password text;\n  v_app_metadata jsonb;\n  v_identity jsonb;\n  v_has_google_identity boolean := false;\nbegin\n  -- Extract encrypted_password first (most reliable indicator of password signup)\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  -- Block password-based signups immediately (they have encrypted_password)\n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Extract provider from multiple possible locations\n  -- 1. raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  \n  -- 2. app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- 3. Check identities array for Google provider (most reliable for OAuth)\n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Allow Google OAuth signups (check both provider variable and identities array)\n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup\n  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",

        "contents": "Use MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Users table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth)\n-- Note: Synced via Next.js server actions, not database triggers\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  email text not null,\n  name text,\n  picture text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\n-- Role enum for profiles (authorization)\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- Focus: Authentication and authorization only\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\n-- Indexes for auth queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Entity Relationships\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────┐\n│   auth.users    │       │    profiles     │\n│  (Supabase)     │       │  (Auth only)    │\n├─────────────────┤       ├─────────────────┤\n│ id (uuid)       │◄──┐   │ id (uuid)       │\n│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation\n-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\n-- This uses SECURITY DEFINER to create a trigger on auth.users table for true server-side enforcement\n-- The trigger runs at the database level and cannot be bypassed by client-side code\n\n-- Create validation trigger function with SECURITY DEFINER\n-- SECURITY DEFINER allows the function to access auth.users table even when called by regular users\n-- This provides true server-side enforcement at the Supabase database level\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_email text;\n  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)",

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  if (\n    request.nextUrl.pathname !== \"/\" &amp;&amp;\n    !user &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/login\") &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/auth\")\n  ) {\n    // no user, potentially respond by redirecting the user to the login page\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // IMPORTANT: You *must* return the supabaseResponse object as it is.\n  // If you're creating a new response object with NextResponse.next() make sure to:\n  // 1. Pass the request in it, like so:\n  //    const myNewResponse = NextResponse.next({ request })\n  // 2. Copy over the cookies, like so:\n  //    myNewResponse.cookies.setAll(supabaseResponse.cookies.getAll())\n  // 3. Change the myNewResponse object to fit your needs, but avoid changing\n  //    the cookies!\n  // 4. Finally:\n  //    return myNewResponse\n  // If this is not done, you may be causing the browser and server to go out\n  // of sync and terminate the user's session prematurely!\n\n  return supabaseResponse;\n}",

        "contents": "  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\n  -- This allows OAuth signups (Google, etc.) to create accounts with any email\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email_change field (where Supabase stores new email during change process)\n  -- This applies to ALL users (both OAuth and email-only)\n  -- OAuth users can sign up, but when they try to add an email identity, it must be CZU domain\n  if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n    v_email_change := NEW.email_change;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email_change is null or empty\n    if v_email_change is not null and v_email_change != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email_change (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email_change, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users, including OAuth users trying to add email identity\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email field if it changed\n  -- For OAuth users: validate when they're changing from OAuth email to a new email\n  -- For email-only users: always validate\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email is null or empty\n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users when changing primary email\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email",

        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "- Delegation to business logic services\n- Logging and observability\n\n**Business Logic** (in service layer):\n- Core business rules and validations\n- Domain-specific operations\n- Data transformations and calculations\n- Business workflow orchestration\n- Domain knowledge and expertise\n\n**Example:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Application Logic (tRPC Procedure)\nexport const createUserProcedure = protectedProcedure\n  .input(createUserSchema)\n  .mutation(async ({ ctx, input }) =&gt; {\n    try {\n      // Application logic: validation, auth, delegation\n      const result = await createUser({\n        userId: ctx.auth.userId,\n        ...input\n      });\n      \n      return { success: true, data: result };\n    } catch (error) {\n      // Application logic: error handling\n      if (error instanceof CustomError) {\n        throw error;\n      }\n      throw new CustomError(\"INTERNAL_ERROR\", \"An unexpected error occurred\");\n    }\n  });\n\n// Business Logic (Service Layer)\nexport const createUser = async (params: CreateUserParams): Promise&lt;User&gt; =&gt; {\n  const { userId, email, name, role } = params;\n  \n  // Business logic: domain rules\n  if (role === 'admin' &amp;&amp; !await hasAdminPrivileges(userId)) {\n    throw new CustomError(\"UNAUTHORIZED\", \"Insufficient privileges for admin role\", 403);\n  }\n  \n  // Business logic: business validations\n  if (await isEmailAlreadyTaken(email)) {\n    throw new CustomError(\"CONFLICT\", \"Email already registered\", 409);\n  }\n  \n  // Business logic: domain operations\n  const user = await userRepo.create({\n    email: email.toLowerCase(),\n    name: name.trim(),\n    role,\n    status: 'pending_verification'\n  });\n  \n  // Business logic: business workflow\n  await sendWelcomeEmail(user);\n  await createDefaultPreferences(user.id);\n  \n  return user;\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### External API Integration\n\n- Isolate external service calls in dedicated modules\n- Implement retry logic with exponential backoff\n- Map provider errors to internal error types\n- Store sensitive data (tokens, keys) securely\n\n## Database &amp;         "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can add an index like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate index userid\non test_table\nusing btree (user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;\n\nYou can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth.uid() = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can do:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions. Wrapping the function causes an &#96;initPlan&#96; to be run by the Postgres optimizer, which allows it to \"cache\" the results per-statement, rather than calling the function on each row.\n\nCaution: You can only use this technique if the results of the query or function do not change based on the row data.\n\n### Minimize joins\n\nYou can often rewrite your Policies to avoid joins between the source and the target table. Instead, try to organize your policy to fetch all the relevant data from the target table into an array or set, then you can use an &#96;IN&#96; or &#96;ANY&#96; operation in your filter.\n\nFor example, this is an example of a slow policy which joins the source &#96;test_table&#96; to the target &#96;team_user&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  (select auth.uid()) in (\n    select user_id\n    from team_user\n    where team_user.team_id = team_id -- joins to the source \"test_table.team_id\"\n  )\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWe can rewrite this to avoid this join, and instead select the filter criteria into a set:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  team_id in (\n    select team_id\n    from team_user",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );",

            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 167

          {
            "lineNumber": 168
          },

          {

            "text": "You can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:",

          {
            "text": "This method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions.         "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",

        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked\n * (not just OAuth providers like Google)\n * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasEmailIdentity(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has an email identity (not just OAuth)\n  // User identities include: email, google, etc.\n  // We need at least one email identity\n  const identities = user.identities || [];\n  \n  // Check if any identity is an email identity (not OAuth)\n  return identities.some(\n    (identity) =&gt; identity.provider === \"email\"\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Handles OAuth callback from Google\n * Exchanges the code for a session and redirects appropriately\n */\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\");\n\n  if (code) {\n    const supabase = await createClient();\n    const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n\n    if (!error) {\n      // Check if user has email identity linked\n      // If not, redirect to verify-email page\n      const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n      const redirectTo = next || (hasEmail ? \"/protected\" : \"/auth/verify-email\");\n      redirect(redirectTo);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to error page if something went wrong\n  redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=Failed to authenticate with Google&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

            "text": "## Helper functions",
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 116
          },
          {
            "text": "Supabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.",
            "lineNumber": 117
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 118
          },
          {
            "text": "### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 119
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "text": "Returns the ID of the user making the request.",
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "Returns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",
            "lineNumber": 127
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useState, useEffect } from \"react\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/client\";\nimport { GoogleLoginButton } from \"@/components/google-login-button\";\nimport { Button } from \"@/components/ui/button\";\nimport { Input } from \"@/components/ui/input\";\nimport { Label } from \"@/components/ui/label\";\nimport {\n  Card,\n  CardContent,\n  CardDescription,\n  CardHeader,\n  CardTitle,\n} from \"@/components/ui/card\";\nimport { Badge } from \"@/components/ui/badge\";\n\n/**\n * Test page for verifying auth restrictions\n * Tests:\n * - Google OAuth signup (should work)\n * - Email/password signup (should be blocked)\n * - OTP email signup (should be blocked)\n * - Email identity addition (should validate CZU domain)\n */\nexport default function AuthTestPage() {\n  const [user, setUser] = useState&lt;any&gt;(null);\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);\n  const [testResults, setTestResults] = useState&lt;{\n    emailPassword?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n    emailOTP?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n    emailIdentity?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n  }&gt;({});\n\n  const supabase = createClient();\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    checkUser();\n    supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(() =&gt; {\n      checkUser();\n    });\n  }, []);\n\n  const checkUser = async () =&gt; {\n    const {\n      data: { user: currentUser },\n    } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n    setUser(currentUser);\n    setLoading(false);\n  };\n\n  const testEmailPasswordSignup = async (e: React.FormEvent&lt;HTMLFormElement&gt;)\n;\n}",

        "contents": "to authenticated\nusing (\n  team_id in (\n    select team_id\n    from team_user\n    where user_id = (select auth.uid()) -- no join\n  )\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Specify roles in your policies\n\nAlways use the Role of inside your policies, specified by the &#96;TO&#96; operator. For example, instead of this query:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on rls_test\nusing ( auth.uid() = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUse:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on rls_test\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis prevents the policy &#96;( (select auth.uid()) = user_id )&#96; from running for any &#96;anon&#96; users, since the execution stops at the &#96;to authenticated&#96; step.",

        "contents": "└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                           │\n                           ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        Supabase                                  │\n│  ┌─────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │   Auth Service      │  │         PostgreSQL              │   │\n│  │  - Google OAuth     │  │  - profiles table               │   │\n│  │  - OTP emails       │  │  - users table                  │   │\n│  │  - Session mgmt     │  │  - No RLS (Next.js handles)     │   │\n│  └─────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────────┘   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n## Simplicity Principles\n\n1. **Business logic in Next.js** - Server actions and middleware handle all rules\n2. **Supabase for storage only** - No hooks, no custom functions, no RLS, just tables\n3. **Minimal components** - Reuse shadcn/ui, no custom abstractions\n4. **Direct database queries** - Query profiles table for verification and access status\n5. **Admin-first onboarding** - Admin creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n\n# Common Traps to Avoid\n\n1. The auth flow will get stuck once the user is redirected back to the nextjs app from supabase.",

            "text": "│  ┌─────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐   │",

        "contents": "await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~40 lines SQL (users, profiles, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (auth logic) | Medium | ~60 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Pending approval page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n| Access revoked page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation\n- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules\n- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         Next.js                                  │",

  "result": "{\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"{\\\"searchDocs\\\":{\\\"nodes\\\":[{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Migrate from Auth0 to Supabase Auth\\\",\\\"href\\\":\\\"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/migrating-to-supabase/auth0\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"# Migrate from Auth0 to Supabase Auth\\\\n\\\\nLearn how to migrate your users from Auth0\\\\n\\\\nYou can migrate your users from Auth0 to Supabase Auth.\\\\n\\\\nChanging authentication providers for a production app is an important operation. It can affect most aspects of your application. Prepare in advance by reading this guide, and develop a plan for handling the key migration steps and possible problems.\\\\n\\\\nWith advance planning, a smooth and safe Auth migration is possible.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Before you begin\\\\n\\\\nBefore beginning, consider the answers to the following questions. They will help you need decide if you need to migrate, and which strategy to use:\\\\n\\\\n*   How do Auth provider costs scale as your user base grows?\\\\n*   Does the new Auth provider provide all needed features? (for example, OAuth, password logins, Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA))\\\\n*   Is downtime acceptable during the migration?\\\\n*   What is your timeline to migrate before terminating the old Auth provider?\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Migration strategies\\\\n\\\\nDepending on your evaluation, you may choose to go with one of the following strategies:\\\\n\\\\n1.  Rolling migration\\\\n2.  One-off migration\\\\n\\\\n| Strategy | Advantages                                                                                     | Disadvantages                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\\\\n| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\\\n| Rolling  | &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;0 downtime&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Users may need to log in again&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;                            | &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Need to maintain 2 different Auth services, which may be more costly in the short-term&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Need to maintain separate codepaths for the period of the migration&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Some existing users may be inactive and have not signed in with the new provider. This means that you eventually need to backfill these users. However, this is a much smaller-scale one-off migration with lower risks since these users are inactive.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt; |\\\\n| One-off  | &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;No need to maintain 2 different auth services for an extended period of time&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt; | &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Some downtime&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Users will need to log in again. Risky for active users.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Migration steps\\\\n\\\\nAuth provider migrations require 2 main steps:\\\\n\\\\n1.  Export your user data from the old provider (Auth0)\\\\n2.  Import the data into your new provider (Supabase Auth)\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1: Export your user data\\\\n\\\\nAuth0 provides two methods for exporting user data:\\\\n\\\\n1.  Use the [Auth0 data export feature](https://auth0.com/docs/troubleshoot/customer-support/manage-subscriptions/export-data)\\\\n2.  Use the [Auth0 management API](https://auth0.com/docs/api/management/v2/users/get-users). This endpoint has a rate limit, so you may need to export your users in several batches.\\\\n\\\\nTo export password hashes and MFA factors, contact Auth0 support.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2: Import your users into Supabase Auth\\\\n\\\\nThe steps for importing your users depends on the login methods that you support.\\\\n\\\\nSee the following sections for how to import users with:\\\\n\\\\n*   [Password-based login](#password-based-methods)\\\\n*   [Passwordless login](#passwordless-methods)\\\\n*   [OAuth](#oauth)\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n#### Password-based methods\\\\n\\\\nFor users who sign in with passwords, we recommend a hybrid approach to reduce downtime:\\\\n\\\\n1.  For new users, use Supabase Auth for sign up.\\\\n2.  Migrate existing users in a one-off migration.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n##### Sign up new users\\\\n\\\\nSign up new users using Supabase Auth's [signin methods](/docs/guides/auth/passwords#signing-up-with-an-email-and-password).\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n##### Migrate existing users to Supabase Auth\\\\n\\\\nMigrate existing users to Supabase Auth. This requires two main steps: first, check which users need to be migrated, then create their accounts using the Supabase admin endpoints.\\\\n\\\\n1.  Get your Auth 0 user export and password hash export lists.\\\\n\\\\n2.  Filter for users who use password login.\\\\n    *   Under the &#96;identities&#96; field in the user object, these users will have &#96;auth0&#96; as a provider. In the same identity object, you can find their Auth0 &#96;user_id&#96;.\\\\n    *   Check that the user has a corresponding password hash by comparing their Auth0 &#96;user_id&#96; to the &#96;oid&#96; field in the password hash export.\\\\n\\\\n3.  Use Supabase Auth's [admin create user](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-createuser) method to recreate the user in Supabase Auth. If the user has a confirmed email address or phone number, set &#96;email_confirm&#96; or &#96;phone_confirm&#96; to &#96;true&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;ts\\\\n    import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\\\n    const supabase = createClient('your_project_url', 'your_supabase_api_key')\\\\n\\\\n    // ---cut---\\\\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({\\\\n      email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n      password_hash: '$2y$10$a9pghn27d7m0ltXvlX8LiOowy7XfFw0hW0G80OjKYQ1jaoejaA7NC',\\\\n      email_confirm: true,\\\\n    })\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n    &lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"note\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Supported password hashing algorithms\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n      Supabase supports bcrypt and Argon2 password hashes.\\\\n    &lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\n    If you have a plaintext password instead of a hash, you can provide that instead. Supabase Auth will handle hashing the password for you. (Passwords are **always** stored hashed.)\\\\n\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;ts\\\\n    import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\\\n    const supabase = createClient('your_project_url', 'your_supabase_api_key')\\\\n\\\\n    // ---cut---\\\\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({\\\\n      email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n      password: 'supersecurepassword123!',\\\\n    })\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n4.  To sign in your migrated users, use the Supabase Auth [sign in methods](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-signinwithpassword).\\\\n\\\\n    To check for edge cases where users aren't successfully migrated, use a fallback strategy. This ensures that users can continue to sign in seamlessly:\\\\n\\\\n    1.  Try to sign in the user with Supabase Auth.\\\\n    2.  If the signin fails, try to sign in with Auth0.\\\\n    3.  If Auth0 signin succeeds, call the admin create user method again to create the user in Supabase Auth.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n#### Passwordless methods\\\\n\\\\nFor passwordless signin via email or phone, check for users with verified email addresses or phone numbers. Create these users in Supabase Auth with &#96;email_confirm&#96; or &#96;phone_confirm&#96; set to &#96;true&#96;:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\\\\nimport { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\\\nconst supabase = createClient('your_project_url', 'your_supabase_api_key')\\\\n\\\\n// ---cut---\\\\nconst { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({\\\\n  email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n  email_confirm: true,\\\\n})\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nCheck your Supabase Auth [email configuration](/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp) and configure your [email template](/dashboard/project/_/auth/templates) for use with magic links. See the [Email templates guide](/docs/guides/auth/auth-email-templates) to learn more.\\\\n\\\\nOnce you have imported your users, you can sign them in using the [&#96;signInWithOtp&#96;](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-signinwithotp) method.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n#### OAuth\\\\n\\\\nConfigure your OAuth providers in Supabase by following the [Social login guides](/docs/guides/auth/social-login).\\\\n\\\\nFor both new and existing users, sign in the user using the [&#96;signInWithOAuth&#96;](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-signinwithoauth) method. This works without pre-migrating existing users, since the user always needs to sign in through the OAuth provider before being redirected to your service.\\\\n\\\\nAfter the user has completed the OAuth flow successfully, you can check if the user is a new or existing user in Auth0 by mapping their social provider id to Auth0. Auth0 stores the social provider ID in the user ID, which has the format &#96;provider_name|provider_id&#96; (for example, &#96;github|123456&#96;). See the [Auth0 identity docs](https://auth0.com/docs/manage-users/user-accounts/identify-users) to learn more.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Mapping between Auth0 and Supabase Auth\\\\n\\\\nEach Auth provider has its own schema for tracking users and user information.\\\\n\\\\nIn Supabase Auth, your users are stored in your project's database under the &#96;auth&#96; schema. Every user has an identity (unless the user is an anonymous user), which represents the signin method they can use with Supabase. This is represented by the &#96;auth.users&#96; and &#96;auth.identities&#96; table.\\\\n\\\\nSee the [Users](/docs/guides/auth/users) and [Identities](/docs/guides/auth/identities) sections to learn more.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Mapping user metadata and custom claims\\\\n\\\\nSupabase Auth provides 2 fields which you can use to map user-specific metadata from Auth0:\\\\n\\\\n*   &#96;auth.users.raw_user_meta_data&#96; : For storing non-sensitive user metadata that the user can update (e.g full name, age, favorite color).\\\\n*   &#96;auth.users.raw_app_meta_data&#96; : For storing non-sensitive user metadata that the user should not be able to update (e.g pricing plan, access control roles).\\\\n\\\\nBoth columns are accessible from the admin user methods. To create a user with custom metadata, you can use the following method:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\\\\nimport { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\\\nconst supabase = createClient('your_project_url', 'your_supabase_api_key')\\\\n\\\\n// ---cut---\\\\nconst { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({\\\\n  email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n  user_metadata: {\\\\n    full_name: 'Foo Bar',\\\\n  },\\\\n  app_metadata: {\\\\n    role: 'admin',\\\\n  },\\\\n})\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"caution\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  These fields will be exposed in the user's access token JWT so it is recommended not to store excessive metadata in these fields.\\\\n&lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\nThese fields are stored as columns in the &#96;auth.users&#96; table using the &#96;jsonb&#96; type. Both fields can be updated by using the admin [&#96;updateUserById&#96; method](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-updateuserbyid). If you want to allow the user to update their own &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; , you can use the [&#96;updateUser&#96; method](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-updateuser).\\\\n\\\\nIf you have a lot of user-specific metadata to store, it is recommended to create your own table in a private schema that uses the user id as a foreign key:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\ncreate table private.user_metadata (\\\\n\\\\tid int generated always as identity,\\\\n\\\\tuser_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\\\\n\\\\tuser_metadata jsonb\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Accordion type=\\\\\\\"default\\\\\\\" openBehaviour=\\\\\\\"multiple\\\\\\\" chevronAlign=\\\\\\\"right\\\\\\\" justified size=\\\\\\\"medium\\\\\\\" className=\\\\\\\"text-foreground-light mt-8 mb-6 [&amp;&gt;div]:space-y-4\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  &lt;AccordionItem header={&lt;span className=\\\\\\\"text-foreground\\\\\\\"&gt;I have IDs assigned to existing users in my database, how can I maintain these IDs?&lt;/span&gt;} id=\\\\\\\"custom-user-id\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    All users stored in Supabase Auth use the UUID V4 format as the ID. If your UUID format is identical, you can specify it in the admin create user method like this:\\\\n\\\\n    &lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"note\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n      New users in Supabase Auth will always be created with a UUID V4 ID by default.\\\\n    &lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;ts\\\\n    // specify a custom id\\\\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({\\\\n      id: 'e7f5ae65-376e-4d05-a18c-10a91295727a',\\\\n      email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n    })\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/AccordionItem&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;AccordionItem header={&lt;span className=\\\\\\\"text-foreground\\\\\\\"&gt;How can I allow my users to retain their existing password?&lt;/span&gt;} id=\\\\\\\"existing-password\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    Supabase Auth never stores passwords as plaintext. Since Supabase Auth supports reading bcrypt and argon2 password hashes, you can import your users passwords if they use the same hashing algorithm. New users in Supabase Auth who use password-based sign-in methods will always use a bcrypt hash. Passwords are stored in the &#96;auth.users.encrypted_password&#96; column.\\\\n  &lt;/AccordionItem&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;AccordionItem header={&lt;span className=\\\\\\\"text-foreground\\\\\\\"&gt;My users have multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled, how do I make sure they don't have to set up MFA again?&lt;/span&gt;} id=\\\\\\\"mfa\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    You can obtain an export of your users' MFA secrets by opening a support ticket with Auth0, similar to obtaining the export for password hashes. Supabase Auth only supports time-based one-time passwords (TOTP). Users who have TOTP-based factors may need to re-enroll using their choice of TOTP-based authenticator instead (e.g. 1Password / Google authenticator).\\\\n  &lt;/AccordionItem&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;AccordionItem header={&lt;span className=\\\\\\\"text-foreground\\\\\\\"&gt;How do I migrate existing SAML Single Sign-On (SSO) connections?&lt;/span&gt;} id=\\\\\\\"saml\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    Customers may need to link their identity provider with Supabase Auth separately, but their users should still be able to sign-in as per-normal after authenticating with their identity provider. For more information about SSO with SAML 2.0, you can check out [this guide](/docs/guides/auth/enterprise-sso/auth-sso-saml). If you want to migrate your existing SAML SSO connections from Auth0 to Supabase Auth, reach out to us via support.\\\\n  &lt;/AccordionItem&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;AccordionItem header={&lt;span className=\\\\\\\"text-foreground\\\\\\\"&gt;How do I migrate my Auth0 organizations to Supabase?&lt;/span&gt;} id=\\\\\\\"migrate-org\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    This isn't supported by Supabase Auth yet.\\\\n  &lt;/AccordionItem&gt;\\\\n&lt;/Accordion&gt;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Useful references\\\\n\\\\n*   [Migrating 125k users from Auth0 to Supabase](https://kevcodez.medium.com/migrating-125-000-users-from-auth0-to-supabase-81c0568de307)\\\\n*   [Loper to Supabase migration](https://eigen.sh/posts/auth-migration)\\\\n\\\"},{\\\"title\\\":\\\"User Management\\\",\\\"href\\\":\\\"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"# User Management\\\\n\\\\nView, delete, and export user information.\\\\n\\\\nYou can view your users on the [Users page](/dashboard/project/_/auth/users) of the Dashboard. You can also view the contents of the Auth schema in the [Table Editor](/dashboard/project/_/editor).\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Accessing user data via API\\\\n\\\\nFor security, the Auth schema is not exposed in the auto-generated API. If you want to access users data via the API, you can create your own user tables in the &#96;public&#96; schema.\\\\n\\\\nMake sure to protect the table by enabling [Row Level Security](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security). Reference the &#96;auth.users&#96; table to ensure data integrity. Specify &#96;on delete cascade&#96; in the reference. For example, a &#96;public.profiles&#96; table might look like this:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\ncreate table public.profiles (\\\\n  id uuid not null references auth.users on delete cascade,\\\\n  first_name text,\\\\n  last_name text,\\\\n\\\\n  primary key (id)\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\nalter table public.profiles enable row level security;\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"caution\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  Only use primary keys as [foreign key references](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-fk.html) for schemas and tables like &#96;auth.users&#96; which are managed by Supabase. Postgres lets you specify a foreign key reference for columns backed by a unique index (not necessarily primary keys).\\\\n\\\\n  Primary keys are **guaranteed not to change**. Columns, indices, constraints or other database objects managed by Supabase **may change at any time** and you should be careful when referencing them directly.\\\\n&lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\nTo update your &#96;public.profiles&#96; table every time a user signs up, set up a trigger. If the trigger fails, it could block signups, so test your code thoroughly.\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- inserts a row into public.profiles\\\\ncreate function public.handle_new_user()\\\\nreturns trigger\\\\nlanguage plpgsql\\\\nsecurity definer set search_path = ''\\\\nas $$\\\\nbegin\\\\n  insert into public.profiles (id, first_name, last_name)\\\\n  values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data -&gt;&gt; 'first_name', new.raw_user_meta_data -&gt;&gt; 'last_name');\\\\n  return new;\\\\nend;\\\\n$$;\\\\n\\\\n-- trigger the function every time a user is created\\\\ncreate trigger on_auth_user_created\\\\n  after insert on auth.users\\\\n  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Adding and retrieving user metadata\\\\n\\\\nYou can assign metadata to users on sign up:\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Tabs scrollable size=\\\\\\\"small\\\\\\\" type=\\\\\\\"underlined\\\\\\\" defaultActiveId=\\\\\\\"js\\\\\\\" queryGroup=\\\\\\\"language\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"js\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"JavaScript\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;js\\\\n    import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\\\n    const supabase = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!)\\\\n\\\\n    // ---cut---\\\\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signUp({\\\\n      email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n      password: 'example-password',\\\\n      options: {\\\\n        data: {\\\\n          first_name: 'John',\\\\n          age: 27,\\\\n        },\\\\n      },\\\\n    })\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"dart\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Dart\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;dart\\\\n    final res = await supabase.auth.signUp(\\\\n      email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',\\\\n      password: 'example-password',\\\\n      data: {\\\\n        'first_name': 'John',\\\\n        'age': 27,\\\\n      },\\\\n    );\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"swift\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Swift\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;swift\\\\n    try await supabase.auth.signUp(\\\\n      email: \\\\\\\"valid.email@supabase.io\\\\\\\",\\\\n      password: \\\\\\\"example-password\\\\\\\",\\\\n      data: [\\\\n        \\\\\\\"first_name\\\\\\\": .string(\\\\\\\"John\\\\\\\"),\\\\n        \\\\\\\"age\\\\\\\": .integer(27),\\\\n      ]\\\\n    )\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"kotlin\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Kotlin\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;kotlin\\\\n    val data = supabase.auth.signUpWith(Email) {\\\\n        email = \\\\\\\"valid.email@supabase.io\\\\\\\"\\\\n        password = \\\\\\\"example-password\\\\\\\"\\\\n        data = buildJsonObject {\\\\n            put(\\\\\\\"first_name\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"John\\\\\\\")\\\\n            put(\\\\\\\"age\\\\\\\", 27)\\\\n        }\\\\n    }\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n&lt;/Tabs&gt;\\\\n\\\\nUser metadata is stored on the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column of the &#96;auth.users&#96; table. To view the metadata:\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Tabs scrollable size=\\\\\\\"small\\\\\\\" type=\\\\\\\"underlined\\\\\\\" defaultActiveId=\\\\\\\"js\\\\\\\" queryGroup=\\\\\\\"language\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"js\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"JavaScript\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;js\\\\n    import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\\\n    const supabase = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!)\\\\n\\\\n    // ---cut---\\\\n    const {\\\\n      data: { user },\\\\n    } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\\\\n    let metadata = user?.user_metadata\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"dart\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Dart\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;dart\\\\n    final User? user = supabase.auth.currentUser;\\\\n    final Map&lt;String, dynamic&gt;? metadata = user?.userMetadata;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"swift\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Swift\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;swift\\\\n    let user = try await supabase.auth.user()\\\\n    let metadata = user.userMetadata\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n\\\\n  &lt;TabPanel id=\\\\\\\"kotlin\\\\\\\" label=\\\\\\\"Kotlin\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;kotlin\\\\n    val user = supabase.auth.retrieveUserForCurrentSession()\\\\n    //Or you can use the user from the current session:\\\\n    val user = supabase.auth.currentUserOrNull()\\\\n    val metadata = user?.userMetadata\\\\n    &#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n  &lt;/TabPanel&gt;\\\\n&lt;/Tabs&gt;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Deleting users\\\\n\\\\nYou may delete users directly or via the management console at Authentication &gt; Users. Note that deleting a user from the &#96;auth.users&#96; table does not automatically sign out a user. As Supabase makes use of JSON Web Tokens (JWT), a user's JWT will remain \\\\\\\"valid\\\\\\\" until it has expired.\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"caution\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  You cannot delete a user if they are the owner of any objects in Supabase Storage.\\\\n\\\\n  You will encounter an error when you try to delete an Auth user that owns any Storage objects. If this happens, try deleting all the objects for that user, or reassign ownership to another user.\\\\n&lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Exporting users\\\\n\\\\nAs Supabase is built on top of Postgres, you can query the &#96;auth.users&#96; and &#96;auth.identities&#96; table via the &#96;SQL Editor&#96; tab to extract all users:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\nselect * from auth.users;\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nYou can then export the results as CSV.\\\\n\\\"},{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Token Security and Row Level Security\\\",\\\"href\\\":\\\"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/token-security\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"# Token Security and Row Level Security\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nWhen you enable OAuth 2.1 in your Supabase project, third-party applications can access user data on their behalf. Row Level Security (RLS) policies are crucial for controlling exactly what data each OAuth client can access.\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"caution\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  **Scopes control OIDC data, not database access**\\\\n\\\\n  The OAuth scopes (&#96;openid&#96;, &#96;email&#96;, &#96;profile&#96;, &#96;phone&#96;) control what user information is included in ID tokens and returned by the UserInfo endpoint. They do **not** control access to your database tables or API endpoints.\\\\n\\\\n  Use RLS to define which OAuth clients can access which data, regardless of the scopes they requested.\\\\n&lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## How OAuth tokens work with RLS\\\\n\\\\nOAuth access tokens issued by Supabase Auth are JWTs that include all standard Supabase claims plus OAuth-specific claims. This means your existing RLS policies continue to work, and you can add OAuth-specific logic to create granular access controls.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Token structure\\\\n\\\\nEvery OAuth access token includes:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"sub\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user-uuid\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"authenticated\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"aud\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"authenticated\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"user_id\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user-uuid\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"email\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user@example.com\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"client_id\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"9a8b7c6d-5e4f-3a2b-1c0d-9e8f7a6b5c4d\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"aal\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"aal1\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"amr\\\\\\\": [{ \\\\\\\"method\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"password\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"timestamp\\\\\\\": 1735815600 }],\\\\n  \\\\\\\"session_id\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"session-uuid\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"iss\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"https://&lt;project-ref&gt;.supabase.co/auth/v1\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"iat\\\\\\\": 1735815600,\\\\n  \\\\\\\"exp\\\\\\\": 1735819200\\\\n}\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nThe key OAuth-specific claim is:\\\\n\\\\n| Claim       | Description                                                    |\\\\n| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |\\\\n| &#96;client_id&#96; | Unique identifier of the OAuth client that obtained this token |\\\\n\\\\nYou can use this claim in RLS policies to grant different permissions to different clients.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Extracting OAuth claims in RLS\\\\n\\\\nUse the &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function to access token claims in your policies:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Get the client ID from the token\\\\n(auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id')\\\\n\\\\n-- Check if the token is from an OAuth client\\\\n(auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NOT NULL\\\\n\\\\n-- Check if the token is from a specific client\\\\n(auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'mobile-app-client-id'\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Common RLS patterns for OAuth\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Pattern 1: Grant specific client full access\\\\n\\\\nAllow a specific OAuth client to access all user data:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Mobile app can access user data\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'mobile-app-client-id'\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Pattern 2: Grant multiple clients read-only access\\\\n\\\\nAllow several OAuth clients to read data, but not modify it:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Third-party apps can read profiles\\\\\\\"\\\\nON profiles FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IN (\\\\n    'analytics-client-id',\\\\n    'reporting-client-id',\\\\n    'dashboard-client-id'\\\\n  )\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Pattern 3: Restrict sensitive data from OAuth clients\\\\n\\\\nPrevent OAuth clients from accessing sensitive data:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"OAuth clients cannot access payment info\\\\\\\"\\\\nON payment_methods FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NULL  -- Only direct user sessions\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Pattern 4: Client-specific data access\\\\n\\\\nDifferent clients access different subsets of data:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Analytics client can only read aggregated data\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Analytics client reads summaries\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_metrics FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'analytics-client-id'\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\n-- Admin client can read and modify all data\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Admin client full access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'admin-client-id'\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Real-world examples\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Example 1: Multi-platform application\\\\n\\\\nYou have a web app, mobile app, and third-party integrations:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Web app: Full access\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Web app full access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON profiles FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (\\\\n    (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'web-app-client-id'\\\\n    OR (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NULL  -- Direct user sessions\\\\n  )\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\n-- Mobile app: Read-only access to profiles\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Mobile app reads profiles\\\\\\\"\\\\nON profiles FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'mobile-app-client-id'\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\n-- Third-party integration: Limited data access\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Integration reads public data\\\\\\\"\\\\nON profiles FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'integration-client-id' AND\\\\n  is_public = true\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Custom access token hooks\\\\n\\\\n[Custom Access Token Hooks](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) work with OAuth tokens, allowing you to inject custom claims based on the OAuth client. This is particularly useful for customizing standard JWT claims like &#96;audience&#96; (&#96;aud&#96;) or adding client-specific metadata.\\\\n\\\\n&lt;Admonition type=\\\\\\\"note\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\n  Custom Access Token Hooks are triggered for **all** token issuance. Use &#96;client_id&#96; or &#96;authentication_method&#96; (&#96;oauth_provider/authorization_code&#96; for OAuth flows) to differentiate OAuth from regular authentication.\\\\n&lt;/Admonition&gt;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Customizing the audience claim\\\\n\\\\nA common use case is customizing the &#96;audience&#96; claim for different OAuth clients. This allows third-party services to validate that tokens were issued specifically for them:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\nimport { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts'\\\\n\\\\nserve(async (req) =&gt; {\\\\n  const { user, claims, client_id } = await req.json()\\\\n\\\\n  // Customize audience based on OAuth client\\\\n  if (client_id === 'mobile-app-client-id') {\\\\n    return new Response(\\\\n      JSON.stringify({\\\\n        claims: {\\\\n          aud: 'https://api.myapp.com',\\\\n          app_version: '2.0.0',\\\\n        },\\\\n      }),\\\\n      { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }\\\\n    )\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  if (client_id === 'analytics-partner-id') {\\\\n    return new Response(\\\\n      JSON.stringify({\\\\n        claims: {\\\\n          aud: 'https://analytics.partner.com',\\\\n          access_level: 'read-only',\\\\n        },\\\\n      }),\\\\n      { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }\\\\n    )\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Default audience for non-OAuth flows\\\\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ claims: {} }), {\\\\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nThe &#96;audience&#96; claim is especially important for:\\\\n\\\\n*   **JWT validation by third parties**: Services can verify tokens were issued for their specific API\\\\n*   **Multi-tenant applications**: Different audiences for different client applications\\\\n*   **Compliance**: Meeting security requirements that mandate audience validation\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Adding client-specific claims\\\\n\\\\nYou can also add custom claims and metadata based on the OAuth client:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\nimport { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts'\\\\nimport { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2'\\\\n\\\\nserve(async (req) =&gt; {\\\\n  const { user, claims, client_id } = await req.json()\\\\n\\\\n  const supabase = createClient(Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!, Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY')!)\\\\n\\\\n  // Add custom claims based on OAuth client\\\\n  let customClaims = {}\\\\n\\\\n  if (client_id === 'mobile-app-client-id') {\\\\n    customClaims.aud = 'https://mobile.myapp.com'\\\\n    customClaims.app_version = '2.0.0'\\\\n    customClaims.platform = 'mobile'\\\\n  } else if (client_id === 'analytics-client-id') {\\\\n    customClaims.aud = 'https://analytics.myapp.com'\\\\n    customClaims.read_only = true\\\\n    customClaims.data_retention_days = 90\\\\n  } else if (client_id?.startsWith('mcp-')) {\\\\n    // MCP AI agents\\\\n    const { data: agent } = await supabase\\\\n      .from('approved_ai_agents')\\\\n      .select('name, max_data_retention_days')\\\\n      .eq('client_id', client_id)\\\\n      .single()\\\\n\\\\n    customClaims.aud = &#96;https://mcp.myapp.com/${client_id}&#96;\\\\n    customClaims.ai_agent = true\\\\n    customClaims.agent_name = agent?.name\\\\n    customClaims.max_retention = agent?.max_data_retention_days\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ claims: customClaims }), {\\\\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nUse these custom claims in RLS:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Policy based on custom claims\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Read-only clients cannot modify\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR UPDATE\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt; 'user_metadata' -&gt;&gt; 'read_only')::boolean IS NOT TRUE\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\n-- Policy based on audience claim\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Only specific audience can access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON api_data FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'aud') IN (\\\\n    'https://api.myapp.com',\\\\n    'https://mobile.myapp.com'\\\\n  )\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Security best practices\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### 1. Principle of least privilege\\\\n\\\\nGrant OAuth clients only the minimum permissions they need:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Bad: Grant all access by default\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"OAuth clients full access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (auth.uid() = user_id);\\\\n\\\\n-- Good: Grant specific access per client\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Specific client specific access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') = 'trusted-client-id'\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### 2. Separate policies for OAuth clients\\\\n\\\\nCreate dedicated policies for OAuth clients rather than mixing them with user policies:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- User access\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Users access their own data\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NULL\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\n-- OAuth client access (separate policy)\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"OAuth clients limited access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IN ('client-1', 'client-2')\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### 3. Regularly audit OAuth clients\\\\n\\\\nTrack and review which clients have access:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- View all active OAuth clients\\\\nSELECT\\\\n  oc.client_id,\\\\n  oc.name,\\\\n  oc.created_at,\\\\n  COUNT(DISTINCT s.user_id) as active_users\\\\nFROM auth.oauth_clients oc\\\\nLEFT JOIN auth.sessions s ON s.client_id = oc.client_id\\\\nWHERE s.created_at &gt; NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'\\\\nGROUP BY oc.client_id, oc.name, oc.created_at;\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Testing your policies\\\\n\\\\nAlways test your RLS policies before deploying to production:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Test as a specific OAuth client\\\\nSET request.jwt.claims = '{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"sub\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"test-user-uuid\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"authenticated\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"client_id\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"test-client-id\\\\\\\"\\\\n}';\\\\n\\\\n-- Test queries\\\\nSELECT * FROM user_data WHERE user_id = 'test-user-uuid';\\\\n\\\\n-- Reset\\\\nRESET request.jwt.claims;\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\nOr use the Supabase Dashboard's [RLS policy tester](/dashboard/project/_/auth/policies).\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Troubleshooting\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Policy not working for OAuth client\\\\n\\\\n**Problem**: OAuth client can't access data despite having a valid token.\\\\n\\\\n**Check**:\\\\n\\\\n1.  Verify the policy includes the client's &#96;client_id&#96;\\\\n2.  Ensure RLS is enabled on the table\\\\n3.  Check for conflicting restrictive policies\\\\n4.  Test with service role key to isolate RLS issues\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Debug: See what client_id is in the token\\\\nSELECT auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id';\\\\n\\\\n-- Debug: Test without RLS\\\\nSET LOCAL role = service_role;\\\\nSELECT * FROM your_table;\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Policy too permissive\\\\n\\\\n**Problem**: OAuth client has access to data it shouldn't.\\\\n\\\\n**Solution**: Use &#96;AS RESTRICTIVE&#96; policies to add additional constraints:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- This policy runs in addition to permissive policies\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Restrict OAuth clients\\\\\\\"\\\\nON sensitive_data\\\\nAS RESTRICTIVE\\\\nFOR ALL\\\\nTO authenticated\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  -- OAuth clients cannot access this table at all\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NULL\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n### Can't differentiate between users and OAuth clients\\\\n\\\\n**Problem**: Need to apply different logic for direct user sessions vs OAuth.\\\\n\\\\n**Solution**: Check if &#96;client_id&#96; is present:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\\\\n-- Direct user sessions (no OAuth)\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"Direct users full access\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR ALL\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NULL\\\\n);\\\\n\\\\n-- OAuth clients (limited access)\\\\nCREATE POLICY \\\\\\\"OAuth clients read only\\\\\\\"\\\\nON user_data FOR SELECT\\\\nUSING (\\\\n  auth.uid() = user_id AND\\\\n  (auth.jwt() -&gt;&gt; 'client_id') IS NOT NULL\\\\n);\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## Next steps\\\\n\\\\n*   [Learn about JWTs](/docs/guides/auth/jwts) - Deep dive into Supabase token structure\\\\n*   [Row Level Security](/docs/guides/auth/row-level-security) - Complete RLS guide\\\\n*   [Custom Access Token Hooks](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) - Inject custom claims\\\\n*   [OAuth flows](/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/oauth-flows) - Understand token issuance\\\\n\\\"}]}}\"}]}"

creates a row in public.users table when a new user is created in auth.users\\n-- This ensures that every authenticated user has a corresponding record in public.users with their Google OAuth data\\n-- Affected tables: public.users\\n-- Special considerations: Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table, extracts Google OAuth metadata\\n\\n-- Create trigger function to populate public.users table when auth.users is created\\n-- Extracts Google OAuth data from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and auth.users.email\\n-- Uses SECURITY DEFINER to allow access to auth.users table\\ncreate or replace function public.handle_new_auth_user()\\nreturns trigger\\nlanguage plpgsql\\nsecurity definer\\nset search_path = ''\\nas $$\\ndeclare\\n  v_google_email text;\\n  v_google_full_name text;\\n  v_google_profile_picture text;\\n  v_raw_meta_data jsonb;\\nbegin\\n  -- Extract raw_user_meta_data (contains Google OAuth profile information)\\n  v_raw_meta_data := new.raw_user_meta_data;\\n  \\n  -- Extract email from auth.users.email (primary email field)\\n  -- Fallback to raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'email' if needed\\n  v_google_email := coalesce(new.email, v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'email');\\n  \\n  -- Extract Google OAuth profile data from raw_user_meta_data\\n  -- Google OAuth typically provides: full_name, avatar_url (or picture), email\\n  v_google_full_name := v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name';\\n  v_google_profile_picture := coalesce(\\n    v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'avatar_url',\\n    v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'picture'\\n  );\\n  \\n  -- Insert new row into public.users table with extracted data\\n  -- auth_user_id links to auth.users.id for authentication checks\\n  insert into public.users (\\n    auth_user_id,\\n    google_email,\\n    google_full_name,\\n    google_profile_picture\\n  )\\n  values (\\n    new.id,\\n    v_google_email,\\n    v_google_full_name,\\n    v_google_profile_picture\\n  );\\n  \\n  return new;\\nend;\\n$$;\\n\\ncomment on function public.handle_new_auth_user() is 'Trigger function that automatically creates a row in public.users table when a new user is created in auth.users. Extracts Google OAuth profile data (email, full_name, profile_picture) from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and populates the public.users table. Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table.';\\n\\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table\\n-- Fires AFTER INSERT to ensure the auth.users row is fully created before populating public.users\\ncreate trigger on_auth_user_created\\nafter insert on auth.users\\nfor each row\\nexecute function public.handle_new_auth_user();\\n\\ncomment on trigger on_auth_user_created on auth.users is 'Trigger that automatically populates public.users table when a new user is created in auth.users via Google OAuth signup.';\"}",

Created and applied the database function and trigger. Summary:

## Summary

Created a database function that runs when a user is created in `auth.users` and populates the `public.users` table with Google OAuth data.

### What was created:

1. **Function: `public.handle_new_auth_user()`**
   - Extracts Google OAuth data from `auth.users.raw_user_meta_data`
   - Populates `public.users` with:
     - `auth_user_id` (links to `auth.users.id`)
     - `google_email` (from `auth.users.email` or metadata)
     - `google_full_name` (from `raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name'`)
     - `google_profile_picture` (from `raw_user_meta_data->>'avatar_url'` or `'picture'`)
   - Uses `SECURITY DEFINER` to access the `auth.users` table
   - Sets `search_path = ''` for security

2. **Trigger: `on_auth_user_created`**
   - Fires `AFTER INSERT` on `auth.users`
   - Executes the function for each new user
   - Enabled and active

### Migration file:
- Created at: `supabase/migrations/20260131150159_create_user_on_auth_user_created.sql`
- Applied to the database

When a new user signs up via Google OAuth, a corresponding row is created in `public.users` with their Google profile information.

The security warnings shown are pre-existing RLS policy warnings and are unrelated to this function.

Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email field if it changed\n  -- For OAuth users: validate when they're changing from OAuth email to a new email\n  -- For email-only users: always validate\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email is null or empty\n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users when changing primary email\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email",
